mira: Starting onboarding for lykos18b-int4 — hitting intermittent OOMs when max_new_tokens >= 512. Seen on both canary and dedicated pools. Anybody seen this pattern before?

sam: Can you paste the exact request shape and batch settings you ran? Also which quantization path (per-channel vs per-tensor)?

mira: Request shape: single-turn chat, prompt ~120 tokens, ask for 600 tokens completion sometimes. We used per-channel int4 conversion from the standard conversion script. Config snippet: ```yaml
model: lykos18b-int4
max_new_tokens: 600
batch_size: 6
coldstart_prefetch: true
kv_prefetch: true
slot_reserve: 0.08
soft_evict_threshold: 0.65
```

kai: Two big suspects: (1) generation window + kv growth for long max_new_tokens, (2) batch packing combining long + short requests causing memory fragmentation. Try lowering batch_size or enabling adaptive windowing.

anuj: Also check kernel scheduling — we saw a similar OOM where microbatching + aggressive prefetch forced larger temporary buffers. Can you share the OOM trace lines?

mira: Pasted logs: ```
[2026-03-18T09:12:10Z] OOM: allocate 1.2GiB while total_free 900MiB
[2026-03-18T09:12:10Z] traceback: runtime.cc:245 allocate_tensor -> kv_cache_extend -> attention_kv_alloc
[2026-03-18T09:12:10Z] ctx: batch 4/6 contained max_new_tokens=600, seq_len grew to 720
```

sam: That seq_len jump is the issue. For int4 models we recommend conservative slot_reserve (>=0.12) when long gens are expected. Your slot_reserve 0.08 leaves little headroom. Try slot_reserve 0.14 + batch_size 3 as a quick test.

kai: Another quick experiment: enable kv_trim_on_eviction: true and set kv_trim_threshold: 0.7 so we proactively compact caches when fragmentation spikes. Also try soft throttle for requests with max_new_tokens > 400.

mira: Will run two canaries: A) slot_reserve=0.14, batch_size=3, B) slot_reserve=0.08, batch_size=6 + kv_trim_on_eviction. ETA 20m.

infra-bot: Canary deploy started for eng-ml/lykos18b-int4 (canary-id: c-20260318-21)

mira: Quick results: A passed 100 sustained requests (no OOM), tail latency +8% but acceptable. B hit OOM after ~17 requests. Detailed perf numbers incoming.

sam: Good signal. Next step: add a generation window cap for public routes: max_new_tokens default -> 400 for lykos18b-int4, with a per-route opt-in override. That prevents accidental large seq_len combos.

aiu: (typo) meant to say anuj: +1 on default cap. Also add a telemetry tag for requests with max_new_tokens > 400 so we can monitor usage.

mira: Agreed. I'll open a quick PR to set model defaults and add a rollout plan: 10% traffic for 24h, then 50% if no regressions. PR will include recommended batch_size=3, slot_reserve=0.14, kv_trim_on_eviction=true.

sam: For the onboarding doc, please add a short note about quantization sensitivity — some layers amplify memory for int4 when sequence grows; we should record which layer ranges caused the biggest KV growth.

mira: Will add layer-level kv growth histogram to the eval harness. Also adding a small eval comparing per-channel vs per-tensor quant paths for memory footprint.

anuj: One more: consider an automated fallback policy in serving — if canary detects repeated OOMs, revert to fp16 variant for that model id for affected sessions. Avoids user-visible 500s.

mira: Noted. I'll draft the fallback policy and add it to the rollout playbook. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Canary deploy finished for eng-ml/lykos18b-int4 (canary-id: c-20260318-21) status=rolled_forward
